_readme: Which database each environment's migrations are allowed to reach.
scripts/migrate-remote.sh takes --env staging|production and refuses unless
the connection it was handed matches the endpoint recorded here. Before this
file existed the script could tell a remote database from a local one and a
pooled host from a direct one, but NOT staging's Neon branch from
production's: both are ep-*.neon.tech and both passed every check. So the
one command that writes said '✅ Applied to ep-…' without ever saying which
environment that was. docs/OUTSTANDING.md §5a is the hour of downtime that
shape of mistake already cost once.
An 'endpoint' is the first label of the hostname with any '-pooler' removed,
so one value covers both the pooled and the direct URL of the same database:
ep-x-y-123-pooler.c-5.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech  ->  ep-x-y-123
ep-x-y-123.c-5.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech         ->  ep-x-y-123
🔴 THIS FIELD TAKES AN ENDPOINT ID, NEVER A CONNECTION STRING. On 20 October
both fields were filled with the full DATABASE_URL copied from the Render
dashboard, passwords included, and pushed — so both database passwords went
into public git history and had to be rotated. That is partly this file's
fault: it says to get the value from 'Environment -> DATABASE_URL', and what
you find there is a connection string. So migrate-remote.sh now REFUSES a
value containing '://' or '@' and says why, and scripts/secret-scan.mjs
fails the commit before it can happen again.
An endpoint id is a hostname fragment and carries no credential:
✅ ep-flat-flower-b1my1tch
🔴 the whole DATABASE_URL, user and password and query string included
Take the DATABASE_URL, keep only the part between '@' and the first '.',
and drop any trailing '-pooler'. Nothing else from that string belongs here.
⚠️ RECORDING A VALUE IS AN ASSERTION, AND IT IS THE ONE STEP NOTHING CAN
CHECK FOR YOU. Nothing here can tell on its own that a given Neon endpoint
is staging rather than production; that is the fact being written down. Get
it from the environment's own service in the Render dashboard (Environment ->
DATABASE_URL on mastande-api for staging, rentboard-api for production) and
paste the endpoint, rather than from whichever shell you last exported. Once
it is right, every run afterwards is checked.
null means 'not recorded yet', and the script REFUSES on it rather than
skipping — an unrecorded environment is the state in which there is no check
at all, so it must not be the state in which the script quietly proceeds.
